finding: The derivative-consistent adaptive representation preserves the analytical nonlinear path and reduces median paired complete Richards solve CPU by about 27.9% on the frozen nonlinear fixture.
scientific_interpretation: A compact shared interpolant for theta and C=dtheta/dh avoids the Newton-path penalty observed when theta and C are approximated independently, while retaining the computational benefit of avoiding repeated analytical constitutive power evaluations.
nonclaims: This is not yet a whole-SWAP speedup claim.
This result is one controlled nonlinear fixture.
next_action: Qualify the same representation prospectively across multiple hydraulic materials, pressure-state regimes, and boundary-condition classes before any production design decision.
